evidence.quote: Many participants suggested that, under their economic outlooks, it would likely be appropriate to keep the target range unchanged for the rest of the year.
participants expressed strongly differing views about what policy decision would most likely be appropriate at the Committee's December meeting.
Many participants, however, remarked that overall inflation had been above target for some time and had shown little sign of returning sustainably to the 2 percent objective in a timely manner.
participants generally judged that upside risks to inflation remained elevated and that downside risks to employment were elevated and had increased since the first half of the year.
almost all participants noted that it was appropriate to conclude the reduction in the Committee's aggregate securities holdings on December 1 or that they could support such a decision.
a labor market that had gradually softened through September and October but had not sharply deteriorated.

parsed.rationale: The minutes record a cut and an end to runoff (dovish), but the forward guidance leans hawkish relative to market pricing of a December cut, with many participants favoring a hold and most warning that further cuts could entrench inflation. Labor weakness and inflation concerns are roughly balanced, leaving a slight net hawkish tilt.
